Somatic amplification operates under a feedback mechanism where external stimuli increase internal emotional intensity, modeled as I × A → E. Bodily leadership establishes a causal hierarchy B → M, suggesting that physiological arousal must precede conscious emotional experience. Sensory gating introduces a threshold-based filter that regulates how much sensory input influences emotional output, represented as G(S) → O. These three operators interact to define emotional dynamics as a nonlinear feedback system with autonomic regulation at its core. Failure modes include sensory overload (amplification breakdown), cognitive dissonance (leadership breakdown), and sensory gating dysfunction (filtering breakdown). The system exhibits emergent properties such as emotional contagion and stress-induced reactivity, which arise from the interplay of these three foundational operators.
